Title: Information on: What were the conditions in the Auschwitz concentr...
The Auschwitz concentration camp, established by Nazi Germany in occupied Poland during World War II, was notoriously known for its harsh and inhumane conditions. Prisoners were subjected to forced labor, malnutrition, and frequent beatings. Living quarters were overcrowded and unsanitary, leading to disease outbreaks. Medical experiments were conducted without anesthesia on prisoners, many of whom died as a result. The most notorious aspect was the mass extermination of six million Jews in gas chambers, with crematories used to dispose of the bodies.
--- End Document 1 ---

final_answer: The Auschwitz concentration camp was established by Nazi Germany in occupied Poland during World War II and was notoriously known for its harsh and inhumane conditions. Prisoners were subjected to forced labor, malnutrition, and frequent beatings. Living quarters were overcrowded and unsanitary, leading to disease outbreaks. Medical experiments were conducted without anesthesia on prisoners, many of whom died as a result. The most notorious aspect was the mass extermination of six million Jews in gas chambers, with crematories used to dispose of the bodies. Albert Speer, the German architect, approved the allocation of materials for the expansion of Auschwitz concentration camp after two of his assistants inspected the facility on a day when almost a thousand Jews were massacred.
